## Purpose
Implements the owner-scoped `/api/user-workflows` CRUD router for saved workflows — a saved workflow is pure data (`base_pipeline_type`, `agent_ids`, `model_overrides`, `selections`) persisted by reusing the existing `workflows` table (`WorkflowDefinition`) as a `source="user"` row. It lets a user save, list, read, update, and delete their own composed agent workflows for later re-launch.

## Shape
- `SaveUserWorkflowRequest` / `UpdateUserWorkflowRequest` / `UserWorkflowResponse` — pydantic request/response schemas.
- `_validate_model_overrides` — allow-list validates `{agent_id: model_id}` against the composition's agents and `ModelCatalog`, mirroring the websocket launch-path check.
- `_compile_selections_trust_user` — re-validates user-authored per-step capability selections by synthesizing a manifest and compiling it with `trust="user"` (server backstop against a tampered/smuggled capability).
- `_project` / `_owned` — row-to-response projection and owner-scoped fetch-or-404 (IDOR protection).
- `create_user_workflow` / `list_user_workflows` / `get_user_workflow` / `update_user_workflow` / `delete_user_workflow` — the five CRUD endpoints, each behind `get_current_user`.

## Why this shape
Every handler re-applies the exact validation predicates the launch path enforces ("save == launch validation", per the module docstring) so a saved row can never contain something launch would reject, while cross-owner access is deliberately mapped to 404 rather than 403 to avoid leaking row existence. The module docstring also states it must never import `agents.execution_engine`, keeping the API layer on the legal `app → agents` dependency direction (ports-and-adapters).
